Main.sentence: The 82nd Airborne Division is an ___E:airborne forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airborne_forces)___ formation of ___E:division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Division_(military))___ -size of the ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ specializing in ___E:parachute assault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paratrooper)___ operations into hostile areas that has remained active since ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ and ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .

The division is commanded by ___E:Major General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_general)___ James "Pat" Work.  It was officially organized in the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ in 25 August 1917 at ___E:Camp Gordon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Gordon)___ in ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , remaining active until 1919, however it was reactivated in 1921, and has now been re-located to ___E:Fort Bragg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Bragg)___ in ___E:North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina)___ .
The 82nd Airborne Division was the second United States infantry-combat division of eight to leave and arrive in England, and fight in France.

When the division ___E:arrived in France U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_II))___ , it came under the command of the ___E:First Allied Airborne Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Allied_Airborne_Army)___ , which controlled all ___E:Allied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II)___ airborne formations.

The 82nd Infantry Division later served with distinction on the ___E:Western Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_I))___ in the final months of ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ .
Since its initial members came from all 48 states, the division acquired the nickname All-American , which is the basis for its "AA" ( pictured ), on the shoulder patch.

The Division took part in the ___E:Battle of Lorraine 1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lorraine)___ , and the campaigns of ___E:St. Mihiel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Mihiel)___ ___E:and Meuse-Argonne 1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse%E2%80%93Argonne_offensive)___ .

It was reconstituted into the ___E:Organized Reserves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Reserve)___ as Headquarters, 82d Division, on 24 June 1921 and was then based at the Federal Building located at ___E:Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia,_South_Carolina)___ , in ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ .

After the ___E:pre-emptive strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preemptive_war)___ on ___E:Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor)___ , in ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ on 7 December 1941 the 82nd Airborne Division would see combat with the command of ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ ___E:General Omar Bradley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Bradley)___ who later on 15 August 1942, reconstituted the 82nd as the first airborne division of the US Army and fought in numerous campaigns during the war.

The 82nd Division was first constituted during ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ on 5 August 1917 as an infantry division in the ___E:National Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_United_States)___ .
It was organized and formally activated on 25 August 1917 at ___E:Camp Gordon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Gordon_(World_War_I))___ , Georgia.
At the time, the division consisted entirely of newly ___E:conscripted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States)___ soldiers.

Original enlisted men assigned to the division came from ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ , ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , and ___E:Tennessee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee)___ , but during October 1917, nearly all of them were transferred to fill shortages in ___E:National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_(United_States))___ and National Army units, principally the ___E:30th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30th_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ , ___E:31st U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ , and ___E:81st Divisions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ , which were training at other camps in the Southern United States.

Replacements for them were received mostly from ___E:Camp Devens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Devens)___ , ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ , ___E:Camp Dix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Dix)___ , ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ , Camps ___E:Lee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Gregg-Adams)___ and ___E:Meade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Meade)___ , ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia)___ , and ___E:Camp Upton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Upton)___ , New York, the men hailing from ___E:New England U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England)___ and the ___E:Mid-Atlantic states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Atlantic_(United_States))___ .

In the spring, 5,000 more replacements for transfers made over the winter were assigned from Fort Devens, Camp Gordon, Camp Upton, ___E:Camp Dodge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Dodge,_Iowa)___ , Iowa, and Camp Travis, ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ , along with a contingent of men from Alabama, Georgia, and Tennessee.

The citizens of ___E:Atlanta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta)___ held a contest to give a nickname to the new division, and in April 1918, ___E:Major General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_general_(United_States))___ ___E:Eben Swift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eben_Swift)___ , the commanding general, chose "All American" to reflect the unique composition of the 82nd—it had soldiers from all 48 states in the Union.
The bulk of the division was two infantry ___E:brigades U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigade)___ , each commanding two regiments.

The 163rd Brigade commanded the ___E:325th Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/325th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ and the ___E:326th Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/326th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ along with the 320th Machine Gun Battalion.

The 164th Brigade commanded the ___E:327th Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/327th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ and the ___E:328th Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/328th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ and the 321st Machine Gun Battalion.

Also in the division were the ___E:157th Field Artillery Brigade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Airborne_Division_Artillery)___ , composed of the ___E:319th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/319th_Field_Artillery_Regiment)___ , ___E:320th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/320th_Field_Artillery_Regiment)___ and ___E:321st Field Artillery Regiments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/321st_Field_Artillery_Regiment)___ and the 307th Trench Mortar Battery; a divisional troops contingent, and a ___E:division train U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_(military))___ .

The division sailed to Europe in May 1918 to join the ___E:American Expeditionary Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Expeditionary_Forces)___ (AEF), commanded by ___E:General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_(United_States))___ ___E:John Pershing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Pershing)___ , on the ___E:Western Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_I))___ .

The 82nd Airborne Division was the first of five airborne divisions (11th, 13th, 17th, 82nd and 101st) to be formed in the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , and was officially activated on 15 August 1942 at Fort Bragg in North Carolina, under the command of ___E:Major General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_general_(United_States))___ Bradley with the classification of an airborne division.

The division's square insignia, is identifiable by an arched red banner embroidered with the letters "AA" (standing for "All American") behind a shade of blue. It serves as the service colors of the United States Army, with red representing artillery and blue for infantry.

A white on blue " ___E:Airborne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airborne_forces)___ " ___E:tab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabs_of_the_United_States_Army#Airborne)___ is worn above the insignia. "All American"  is the nickname given to the division when it was first formed at Camp Gordon, Georgia, in 1917, submitted by Vivienne Goodwyn.
The insignia was approved in 1918 during ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ .

The double “A” refers to the nickname “All American Division” adopted by the organization during World War I. The newly form unit was composed of members, who came from all across all 48 states and given the nickname “All-American.” The shoulder sleeve insignia was redesigned for the 82nd Airborne Division and an Airborne tab was added on top, authorized on August 31, 1942.

Brigadier General ___E:William P. Burnham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_P._Burnham)___ , who had previously commanded the 164th Brigade, led the division during most of its training and movement to Europe.

In early April 1918, the division embarked from the ports in ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ , New York City and ___E:Brooklyn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn)___ to ___E:Liverpool U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool)___ , England, where the division fully assembled by mid-May 1918.  From there, the division moved to ___E:Continental Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Europe)___ , leaving ___E:Southampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton)___ and arriving at ___E:Le Havre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Havre)___ , France.

The 82nd Division then moved to the British-controlled sector of the ___E:Somme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somme_(department))___ , where it began sending small numbers of troops and officers to the front lines to gain combat experience.
On 16 June, it moved by ___E:rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railroad)___ to the French sector.

The division was briefly assigned to ___E:I Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Corps_(United_States))___ before falling under the command of ___E:IV Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IV_Corps_(United_States))___ until late August.
It was then moved to the ___E:Woëvre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wo%C3%ABvre)___ front.

As part of the American Expeditionary Forces (AEF) deployed during WWI, the 82nd Division began training with British forces in Picardy as early as 10 May 1918. From there they moved to the hotly contested French border region of ___E:Lorraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorraine)___ , which they occupied from 16 June to 11 September in preparation for the ___E:Saint-Mihiel offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Saint-Mihiel)___ .

As the attack on the Saint-Mihiel salient began on 12 September, the division engaged in a holding mission to prevent ___E:Imperial German Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_German_Army)___ forces from attacking the right flank of the First Army. This defensive action allowed the 163rd Brigade and 327th Infantry Regiment to advance north-east, raiding the communes of ___E:Port-sur-Seille U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-sur-Seille)___ , ___E:Eply U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eply)___ , ___E:Bois de Cheminot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bois_de_Cheminot)___ , and ___E:Bois Fréhaut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bois_Fr%C3%A9haut)___ .

Meanwhile, the 328th Infantry Regiment advanced on the west of the ___E:Moselle River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moselle_River)___ , made contact with the ___E:90th Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90th_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ , and entered the town of ___E:Norroy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norroy-l%C3%A8s-Pont-%C3%A0-Mousson)___ , to consolidate American troop positions.
By 17 September, the Saint-Mihiel offensive had stabilized, and preparations for the infamous ___E:Meuse-Argonne offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse%E2%80%93Argonne_offensive)___ began.
On 20 September, the 82nd Division was relieved by the French 69th Division.

The 82nd Division was then stationed near ___E:Triaucourt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triaucourt)___ and ___E:Rarécourt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rar%C3%A9court)___ , near the First Army.  During this operation, the 82nd Division suffered casualties from heavy artillery fire which the fresh American soldiers were completely unused to. The division was moved into reserve from 26 September to 3 October while it assembled near ___E:Varennes-en-Argonne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varennes-en-Argonne)___ to train and prepare for the ___E:Meuse-Argonne offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meuse%E2%80%93Argonne_offensive)___ .

The division mobilized to the ___E:Clermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clermont-en-Argonne)___ area in Argonne (just west of Verdun) starting on 24 September, stationed there to act as a reserve for the US First Army.  On 3 October, Major General ___E:George B. Duncan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_B._Duncan)___ , commander of the 77th Division, relieved William Burnham of his duties and took over as commander of the 82nd.

On the night of 6 October 1918, the 164th Brigade relieved troops of the ___E:28th Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28th_Division_(United_States))___ , which were holding the front line from south of ___E:Fléville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fl%C3%A9ville)___ to ___E:La Forge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Forge,_Vosges)___ , along the eastern bank of the ___E:Aire River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aire_(Aisne))___ .

On 7 October the 82nd Division, minus the 163rd Brigade, which remained in reserve, attacked the northeastern edge of the ___E:Argonne Forest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_of_Argonne)___ , taking "Hill 223" in the process.
The division's right flank entered the commune of ___E:Cornay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornay)___ but later withdrew southeast.
The division's left flank took the high ground northwest of ___E:Châtel-Chéhéry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2tel-Ch%C3%A9h%C3%A9ry)___ .
On 9 October, the division's left flank advanced to form a line along the French pylons on the road to the Belgian city of ___E:la Louvière U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Louvi%C3%A8re)___ .
Throughout October, the division advanced north-east along the ___E:Aire (Aisne) river U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aire_(Aisne))___ .

On 10 October, it relieved troops of the ___E:1st Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ in Ardennes at ___E:Fléville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fl%C3%A9ville)___ and ___E:Sommerance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommerance)___ .

The 82nd Division then relaunched an attack on ___E:Cornay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornay)___ and the Belgian city of ___E:Enghien U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enghien)___ , successfully re-establishing the front there.

On 11 October, the right flank of the division took the high ground north of the ___E:Rance river U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rance_(river))___ while the left flank continued to advance along the Aire. The next day, the ___E:42nd Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42nd_Division_(United_States))___ relieved the 82nd's troops in Sommerance.
Attacking with fresh troops, the 82nd broke through the ___E:Hindenburg line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindenburg_line)___ on 15 October.

On 18 October, the 82nd Division relieved the ___E:78th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/78th_Division_(United_States))___ division at ___E:Champigneulle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champigneulle)___ .
Three days later it advanced to the Ravin aux Pierres.

On 31 October, the 82nd, except the artillery, was relieved by the ___E:77th Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/77th_Sustainment_Brigade)___ and the ___E:80th Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/80th_Division_(United_States))___ , and assembled in the ___E:Argonne Forest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_of_Argonne)___ to regroup.

On 10 November, it moved again to training areas in ___E:Bourmont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourmont)___ , where it remained until the ___E:Armistice of 11 November 1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_11_November_1918)___ .
The division suffered 995 killed and 7,082 wounded, for a total of 8,077 casualties.

Following the war's end, the division moved to training areas near ___E:Prauthoy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prauthoy)___ , where it remained through February 1919.  It returned to the United States in April and May, and was ___E:demobilized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demobilized)___ and deactivated at ___E:Camp Mills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Mills,_New_York)___ , New York, on 27 May.

Pursuant to the ___E:National Defense Act of 1920 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defense_Act_of_1920)___ , the 82nd Division was reconstituted in the ___E:Organized Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Reserve)___ on 24 June 1921, allotted to the Fourth ___E:Corps Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_Area)___ , assigned to the ___E:XIV Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XIV_Corps_(United_States))___ , and further allotted to Florida, ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , and ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ as its home area. The division headquarters was organized on 23 September 1921 at 1202-1/2 Main Street in ___E:Columbia, South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia,_South_Carolina)___ , relocating in 1923 to the Post Office Building where it remained until activated for World War II.

The 82nd Division's designated mobilization station was ___E:Camp McClellan, Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_McClellan,_Alabama)___ , also where much of the unit's annual training activities occurred in the interwar years.

The headquarters usually trained at Camp McClellan, but also occasionally trained with the staff of the ___E:8th Infantry Brigade, 4th Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ .

The 82nd Division's infantry regiments held their annual training primarily with the units of the 8th Infantry Brigade, while other units, such as the special troops, artillery, engineers, aviation, medical, and quartermaster units, usually trained alongside the active elements of the 4th Division at various posts in the Fourth Corps Area. For example, the division artillery trained with the units of the 13th Field Artillery Brigade at ___E:Fort Bragg, North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Bragg,_North_Carolina)___ ; the 307th Engineer Regiment alongside Company A, 4th Engineer Regiment at ___E:Fort Benning, Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Benning,_Georgia)___ ; the 307th Medical Regiment trained at the medical officers training camp at ___E:Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Oglethorpe,_Georgia)___ ; and the 307th Observation Squadron with Air Corps units at ___E:Maxwell Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Air_Force_Base)___ , Alabama.

The infantry regiments of the division rotated responsibility to conduct the ___E:Citizens' Military Training Camps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizens%27_Military_Training_Camp)___ each year at Camp McClellan.

The division participated in Fourth Corps Area or Third Army command post exercises in conjunction with other Regular Army, National Guard and Organized Reserve units, but unlike Regular and Guard units, the 82nd Division did not participate as an organized unit in the Fourth Corps Area maneuvers and the ___E:Third Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Central)___ maneuvers of 1938, 1940, and 1941 due to a lack of enlisted personnel and equipment, with the officers and a few enlisted reservists assigned to fill vacant slots in organized units to bring them to war strength for the exercises, with others assigned duties as umpires or support personnel.
Before Organized Reserve infantry divisions were ordered into active military service, they were reorganized on paper as "triangular" divisions under the 1940 tables of organization.
The headquarters companies of the two infantry brigades were consolidated into the division's cavalry reconnaissance troop, and one infantry regiment was removed by inactivation.

The field artillery brigade headquarters and headquarters battery became the headquarters and headquarters battery of the division artillery, and its three field artillery regiments were reorganized into four battalions.
The engineer, medical, and quartermaster regiments were reorganized into battalions.

In 1942, divisional quartermaster battalions were split into ordnance light maintenance companies and quartermaster companies, and the division's headquarters and military police company, which had previously been a combined unit, was split.

The 82nd Division was redesignated on 13 February 1942 as Division Headquarters, 82nd Division, and ordered into active service on 25 March 1942, at ___E:Camp Claiborne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Claiborne)___ , ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , under the command of ___E:Major General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_general_(United_States))___ ___E:Omar N. Bradley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Bradley)___ .

The officer and enlisted cadre mostly came from the ___E:9th Infantry Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Infantry_Division_(United_States))___ , while the enlisted fillers came from reception centers in the ___E:Midwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States)___ , ___E:South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States)___ , and ___E:Southwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States)___ .

During this period, the division brought together three officers who would ultimately steer the US Army during the following two decades: ___E:Matthew Ridgway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Ridgway)___ , ___E:James M. Gavin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_M._Gavin)___ , and ___E:Maxwell D. Taylor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_D._Taylor)___ .

Under Major General Bradley, the 82nd Division's ___E:Chief of staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_staff)___ was ___E:George Van Pope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_Van_Pope&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

On 15 August 1942, the 82nd Infantry Division, now commanded by Major General Ridgway, became the first airborne division in the history of the US Army, and was redesignated as the 82nd Airborne Division .

The 82nd was selected after deliberations by the US Army General Staff because of a number of factors; it was not a Regular Army or National Guard unit (historian John B. Wilson wrote that "many traditionalists in those components wanted nothing to do with such an experimental force," while James M. Gavin wrote that many states would refuse the conversion of their National Guard units, likely because of the additional expenses needed to maintain facilities for airborne units), its personnel had all completed basic training, and it was stationed in an area that had good weather and flying facilities.

The division initially consisted of the ___E:325th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/325th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ , ___E:326th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/326th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ and ___E:327th Infantry Regiments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/327th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ , and supporting units.

The 327th was soon transferred to help form the ___E:101st Airborne Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/101st_Airborne_Division)___ and was replaced by the ___E:504th Parachute Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/504th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ , leaving the division with two regiments of ___E:glider infantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glider_infantry)___ and one of ___E:parachute infantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paratrooper)___ .

In February 1943 the division received another change when the 326th was transferred to the ___E:13th Airborne Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_Airborne_Division_(United_States))___ , being replaced by the ___E:505th Parachute Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/505th_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ , under James M. Gavin, then a ___E:colonel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_(United_States))___ , who was later to command the division.

In April 1943, ___E:paratroopers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paratrooper)___ from the 82nd, under the command of Major General ___E:Ridgway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Ridgway)___ , sailed into the ___E:Mediterranean Theater of Operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Theater_of_Operations)___ and landed in North Africa as part of the Allied plan to ___E:invade Sicily U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily)___ .

The division's first two combat operations were ___E:parachute assaults U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paratrooper)___ into Sicily on 9 July and ___E:Salerno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Italy#Salerno_landings)___ on 13 September 1943.  The initial assault on Sicily, by the 505th Parachute Regimental Combat Team, under Colonel Gavin, was the first regimental-sized combat parachute assault conducted by the United States Army. [citation needed] The first glider assault did not occur until ___E:Operation Neptune U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_landings)___ as part of the ___E:D-Day landings of 6 June 1944 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_landings)___ .
Troopers arrived in Italy by ___E:landing craft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landing_craft)___ at Maiori, Naples, and Salerno.

During the ___E:invasion of Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Italy)___ , Ridgway considered ___E:Will Lang Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Lang_Jr.)___ of ___E:TIME magazine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine))___ an honorary member of the division.

In January 1944, the 504th, commanded by ___E:Colonel Reuben Tucker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Henry_Tucker_III)___ , which was temporarily detached to ___E:fight at Anzio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Anzio)___ , adopted the nickname "Devils in Baggy Pants", taken from an entry in a German officer's diary.

With two air drops under its belt, the 82nd Airborne was ready for the second "D-Day" operation in the division's history; ___E:Operation Neptune U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_landings)___ , or the amphibious assault portion of Allied ___E:invasion of Normandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Normandy)___ .

The division conducted ___E:Mission Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Boston)___ , a component of the ___E:Operation Overlord U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Overlord)___ plan.

During the 6 June assault, a 508th platoon leader, ___E:First lieutenant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_lieutenant)___ ___E:Robert P. Mathias U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_P._Mathias)___ , would be the first US Army officer killed by German fire during the invasion.

DeGlopper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_N._DeGlopper)___ of the 325th GIR.  When the division was relieved in early July, the 82nd had seen a month straight of severe combat.

The Germans pursued their retreat with the 2nd and 9th SS Panzer Divisions.

The failure of the 9th and 2nd SS Panzer Divisions to break through the 82nd lines marked the end of the German offensive in the northern shoulder of the Bulge.
The German objective now became one of defense.
On 3 January 1945, the 82nd Airborne Division conducted a counterattack.

On the first day's fighting the 82nd Airborne overran the ___E:62nd Volksgrenadiers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/62nd_Volksgrenadier_Division_(Wehrmacht))___ and the 9th SS Panzer's positions capturing 2,400 prisoners.

The few soldiers who remained were later absorbed into units of the 82nd Airborne.
After several days of fighting, the destruction of the 62nd Volksgrenadiers, and what had been left of the 9th SS Panzer Division was complete.
For the 82nd Airborne Division the first part of the Battle of the Bulge had ended.

The deployment of the 3rd Brigade took place with significant problems and controversy.

In The Rise and Fall of an American Army: US Ground Forces in Vietnam, 1965–1973, author Shelby L. Stanton describes how, other than the 82nd, only two under-strength Marine and four skeletonized Army divisions were left stateside by the beginning of 1968. The ___E:U.S. Military Assistance Command, Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Assistance_Command,_Vietnam)___ (MACV), desperate for additional manpower, wanted the division to deploy to Vietnam, and the Department of the Army, wishing to retain its "sole readily deployable strategic reserve, the last real vestige of actual Army divisional combat potency in the United States left to the Pentagon," compromised by sending the 3d Brigade.
As Stanton wrote:
The division had been so rushed to get this brigade to the battlefront that it ignored individual deployment criteria.

Paratroopers who had just returned from Vietnam now found themselves suddenly going back. The howl of soldier complaints was so vehement that the Department of the Army was soon forced to give each trooper who had deployed to Vietnam with the 3d Brigade the option of returning to Fort Bragg or remaining with the unit. To compensate for the abrupt departures from home for those who elected to stay with the unit, the Army authorized a month leave at the soldiers' own expense or a two-week leave with government aircraft provided for special flights back to North Carolina.

Of the 3,650 paratroopers who had deployed from Fort Bragg, 2,513 elected to return to the United States at once. MACV had no paratroopers to replace them, and overnight the brigade was transformed into a separate light infantry brigade, airborne in name only.

On 20 December 1989, the "All-American", as part of the ___E:United States invasion of Panama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Panama)___ , conducted their first combat jump since World War II onto ___E:Torrijos International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tocumen_International_Airport)___ , Panama.

The goal of the 1st Brigade task force, which was made up of the 1–504th and 2–504th INF as well as 4–325th INF and Company A, 3–505th INF, and 3–319th FAR, was to oust ___E:Manuel Noriega U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Noriega)___ from power.
They were joined on the ground by 3–504th INF, which was already in Panama.

The invasion was initiated with a night combat jump and airfield seizures; the 82nd conducted follow-on combat air assault missions in ___E:Panama City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_City)___ and the surrounding areas of the Gatun Locks.

The operation continued with an assault of multiple strategic installations, such as the Punta Paitilla Airport in Panama City and a ___E:Panamanian Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panamanian_Public_Forces)___ (PDF) garrison and airfield at ___E:Rio Hato U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%ADo_Hato)___ , where Noriega also maintained a residence.

The attack on La Comandancia (PDF HQ) touched off several fires, one of which destroyed most of the adjoining and heavily populated El Chorrillo neighborhood in downtown Panama City. The 82nd Airborne Division secured several other key objectives such as Madden Dam, El Ranacer Prison, Gatun Locks, Gamboa and Fort Cimarron.

Overall, the operation involved 27,684 US troops and over 300 aircraft, including C-130 Hercules, AC-130 Spectre gunship, OA-37B Dragonfly observation, and attack aircraft, C-141 and C-5 strategic transports, F-117A Nighthawk stealth aircraft and AH-64 Apache attack helicopters.
The invasion of Panama was the first combat deployment for the AH-64, the HMMWV, and the F-117A.

In the short six years since the ___E:Invasion of Grenada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Urgent_Fury)___ , Operation Just Cause demonstrated how quickly the US Armed Forces could adapt and overcome the mistakes and equipment interoperability issues to conduct a quick and decisive victory.
In all, the 82nd Airborne Division suffered six of the 23 fatalities of the operation.
The paratroopers began redeployment to Fort Bragg on 12 January 1990. Operation Just Cause concluded on 31 January 1990, just 42 days (D+42) since the invasion started. [citation needed]

The DRF 2 and 3 (1–325 and 2-325 INF, respectively) began drawing the "line in the sand" near al Jubail by building defenses for possible retrograde operations.

There, intensive intelligence operations began in anticipation of desert fighting against the heavily armored ___E:Iraqi Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Army)___ .

In the coming weeks using primarily the 5-Ton cargo trucks of these NG truck companies, the 1st Brigade moved north to "tap line road" in the vicinity of ___E:Rafha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafha)___ , Saudi Arabia.

Extensive ground operations began almost six weeks later.

The 2–325th INF was the division's spearhead for the ground war who took positions over the Iraqi border 24 hours in advance of U.N. coalition forces at 8:00 am, 22 February 1991, on Objectives Tin Man and Rochambeau.

On 23 February, 82nd Airborne Division paratroopers protected the ___E:XVIII Airborne Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XVIII_Airborne_Corps_(United_States))___ flank as fast-moving armor and mechanized units moved deep inside south-western Iraq. The 82nd drove deep into Iraq and captured thousands of Iraqi soldiers and tons of equipment, weapons, and ammunition.
During that time, the 82nd's band and MP company processed 2,721 prisoners.
After the liberation of ___E:Kuwait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait)___ and the surrender of the Iraqi Army, the 82nd redeployed to Fort Bragg. [citation needed]

But it did get a little close there for a while.

[citation needed]

According to accounts of 82nd Airborne officers and NCOs, members of the battalion in 2003–2004 routinely used physical and mental torture as a means of intelligence gathering and for stress relief.

According to the report, these battalion members estimated "...that about half of the detainees at Camp Mercury were released because they were not involved in the insurgency, but they left with the physical and mental scars of torture."

After reporting these abuses yet being ignored by his superiors for 17 months, a then-anonymous captain took his allegations to three senior Republican senators— ___E:Bill Frist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Frist)___ , ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ , and ___E:John Warner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Warner)___ —before the Army was finally compelled to launch an investigation.

The 1st Battalion, ___E:504th Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/504th_Infantry_Regiment)___ 's torture and abuse of prisoners later inspired the passage of the ___E:Detainee Treatment Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detainee_Treatment_Act)___ , and the anonymous captain was later revealed to be ___E:Ian Fishback U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Fishback)___ .

Major Fishback's courageous letter shed light on the atrocities that were being committed—shamefully—in the name of our nation. ...

After reports emerged from horrific abuses at Abu Ghraib in Iraq, I tried for a year and a half to pass legislation to make it clear that cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment of detainees was illegal.
Two military heroes, my former colleague Senator John McCain and Major Fishback, turned the tide in this effort.

In December 2008, the 3d BCT deployed to Baghdad, Iraq and redeployed to Ft. Bragg in November 2009. In August 2009, 1st BCT deployed once again to Iraq and redeployed late July 2010.
During the months of August and September 2009, 4th BCT deployed again to Afghanistan and returned in August 2010 having lost 38 soldiers. [citation needed]
In May 2011 1–505 (Task Force 1 Panther) deployed to Afghanistan in support of ___E:Operation Enduring Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Enduring_Freedom)___ .
Dispersed throughout the country, 1st battalion was attached to various Special Operations elements. 1st battalion redeployed to Fort Bragg, NC in February 2012 having lost two paratroopers.

The 2d Brigade deployed to the ___E:Anbar Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Anbar_Governorate)___ in Iraq in May 2011 for the last time in support of ___E:Operation New Dawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_New_Dawn_(Iraq,_2010-2011))___ with the mission to advise, train and assist the ___E:Iraqi security forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_security_forces)___ and lead the responsible withdrawal of ___E:US Forces – Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Forces_%E2%80%93_Iraq)___ .
Elements of 2d Brigade were among the last US combat units to withdraw from Baghdad.

The brigade suffered the loss of the last American service member in Iraq, SPC. David E. Hickman, on 14 November 2011. They were part of the long convoy of equipment and troops who exited Iraq into Kuwait as OIF came to an end.

As part of ___E:Operation Unified Response U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Unified_Response)___ , the 2d BCT, on rotation as the division's Global Response Force, was alerted and deployed forces to Haiti later that same day for the mission to provide humanitarian assistance following the devastating earthquake in Haiti.
Paratroopers distributed water and food during the ___E:2010 Haiti earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake)___ relief.

Just two months following redeployment from Haiti in 2010, elements of 2d BCT (Red Falcons) deployed to Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom to serve as trainers for the Afghan National Security Forces.
In October 2011, the Division Headquarters returned to Afghanistan, where they relieved the 10th Mountain Division as the Headquarters of Regional Command-South.
In February 2012, 4th BCT deployed to Kandahar province.
Taliban commander Mullah Dadullah, formed an overwhelming force in Kandahar.

Zhari district in southern Kandahar is where Dadullah was recruiting a high number of jihadists. 4th BCT of the 82nd held the 5-month siege from March 2012 to the end of July, witnessing some of the most intense combat since the initial deployments since 2001, 4th BCT inflicted massive casualties among the Taliban.
Performing with an almost perfect strategic plan, 4th BCT drove Dadullah and his men out of Kandahar to the Northeastern province of Kunar, where Dadullah was killed by airstrikes. [citation needed]

As of April 2012, the 1st BCT was deployed to Afghanistan, operating in ___E:Ghazni Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazni_Province)___ , Regional Command-East. The paratroopers took control of Ghazni from the ___E:Polish Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Armed_Forces)___ , allowing the Polish Task Force White Eagle ( ___E:pl:Polski Kontyngent Wojskowy w Afganistanie U:(https://pl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polski_Kontyngent_Wojskowy_w_Afganistanie)___ ) to consolidate around the provincial seat in northern Ghazni.
In June 2012, the 3rd Brigade Combat Team deployed as part of the Global Response Force (GRF) in support of heavy combat operations conducted by the 1st Infantry Division.
The Brigade was spread across much of RC-East Afghanistan.

In December 2013, elements of the 4th Brigade deployed again to Afghanistan and they were joined by the 1st Brigade in spring 2014.  Since 11 September 2001, the division has lost 106 paratroopers in Afghanistan and 139 paratroopers in Iraq. [citation needed]

On 19 December 2014, Stars & Stripes, a daily military newspaper, announced 1,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne's 3rd Brigade Combat Team would deploy to Iraq to train, advise, and assist Iraq's Security Forces.

On 3 November 2016, it was reported that 1,700 soldiers from the 2d Brigade Combat Team will deploy to the US Central Command area of responsibility in Iraq, to take part in ___E:Operation Inherent Resolve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Inherent_Resolve)___ .

They will replace the 2d Brigade Combat Team, ___E:101st Airborne Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/101st_Airborne_Division)___ and will advise and assist Iraqi Security Forces currently trying to ___E:retake Mosul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mosul_(2016))___ from ___E:ISIS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIS)___ fighters.

On 27 March 2017, it was reported that 300 paratroopers from the 82nd Airborne's 2nd Brigade Combat Team will temporarily deploy to northern Iraq to provide additional advise-and-assist combating ___E:ISIS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State)___ , particularly to speed up the ___E:offensive against ISIS in Mosul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mosul_(2016%E2%80%932017))___ .

On 31 December 2019, approximately 750 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne's Immediate Response Force were authorized to be deployed to Iraq in response to events which saw the ___E:United States' embassy in the country stormed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_the_United_States_embassy_in_Baghdad)___ .
From the start of January 2017 to September 2017, the division suffered the loss of five paratroopers killed in action.
It was confirmed in July 2020 that the 82nd Airborne Division did in fact have combat deployments in Syria.

The 1st BCT deployed to Afghanistan in support of ___E:Operation Freedom's Sentinel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%93present)#Post_ISAF_phase)___ from June 2017 to March 2018.    Two soldiers were killed in action when their convoy was purposefully hit by a vehicle filled with explosives.

The 3rd BCT deployed to Afghanistan in support of ___E:Operation Freedom's Sentinel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%93present)#Post_ISAF_phase)___ from July 2019 to March 2020. In February 2020 soldiers from the ___E:1st BCT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Brigade_Combat_Team,_10th_Mountain_Division_(United_States))___ , ___E:10th Mountain Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10th_Mountain_Division)___ were deployed to Afghanistan to replace the 3rd BCT as part of a unit rotation.

The 82nd Airborne was called to deploy in Iraq upon after ___E:rioting civilians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_the_United_States_embassy_in_Baghdad)___ outside of the ___E:US embassy in Baghdad, Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_the_United_States,_Baghdad)___ breached the outer gates of the Green Zone. On 1 January 2020, the first 750 troops began mobilizing to Kuwait and bases in the Baghdad area. On the direct orders of Donald Trump, Iranian general and ___E:Quds Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quds_Force)___ commander ___E:Qasem Soleimani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qasem_Soleimani)___ was killed in a ___E:US airstrike at the Baghdad airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Baghdad_International_Airport_airstrike)___ .
Iranian influence on Iraqi militia groups was believed to play a part in the rioting at the US embassy.

Actions by the Iranians and the US have increased tensions in the region not seen since before the invasion of Iraq in 2003. The 82nd airborne was among the first military units to be mobilized in response to this escalation and tensions.
An additional 3,500 to 4,000 troops were ordered to deploy to Kuwait in response to Iranian threats in the region.  [non-primary source needed]

In August 2021, elements of the 82nd Airborne Division, particularly the ___E:Immediate Response Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immediate_Response_Force)___ , deployed to Afghanistan to secure the evacuation of American diplomats and Afghan Special Immigrant Visa applicants as the Taliban seized land and converged on Kabul.
Throughout ___E:Operation Allies Refuge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Allies_Refuge)___ , the 82nd Airborne Division served as the Operational Command, Task Force 82.

Operation Allies Refuge, led by Major General Chris Donahue, was a combined and joint NATO command post composed of forces representing NATO allied Nations, 1st Brigade Combat Team "Devil", aviation capabilities from the 82nd Combat Aviation Brigade "Pegasus", medical capabilities from the 44th Medical Brigade, riot control capabilities from the 16th Military Police Brigade, 24th Marine Expeditionary Unit, and the 3rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command who oversaw sustainment in the joint operational area from a command post in Kuwait.

The 82nd Airborne Division consists of a division headquarters and headquarters battalion, three infantry brigade combat teams, a division artillery, a combat aviation brigade, and a division sustainment brigade.
The 82nd DIVARTY commands all artillery battalions.

The division's 4th Brigade Combat Team inactivated in fall of 2013: the Special Troops Battalion, 4th Brigade Combat Team;  the 2nd Battalion, ___E:321st Field Artillery Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/321st_Field_Artillery_Regiment_(United_States))___ ; and the 782nd Brigade Support Battalion were inactivated with some of the companies of the 782nd used to augment support battalions in the remaining three brigades.

The 4th Squadron, 73rd Cavalry joined the 1st Brigade Combat Team and formed the core of the newly activated 2nd Battalion, ___E:501st Infantry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501st_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States))___ .
The 2nd Battalion, 508th Infantry Regiment joined the 2nd Brigade Combat Team, while the 1st Battalion, 508th Infantry Regiment joined the 3rd Brigade Combat Team. [citation needed]

To commemorate the 1944 ___E:Waal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waal_(river))___ assault river crossing made by the 504th Parachute Infantry Regiment and the 307th Engineer Battalion (Airborne) during ___E:Operation Market Garden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Market_Garden)___ , an annual Crossing of the Waal competition is staged on the anniversary of the operation at McKellar's Lake near Fort Bragg.
The winning company receives a ___E:paddle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddle)___ .
